One-point deduction because bash -n stderr is redirected to /dev/null (hiding failure diagnostics) and bundle evidence cannot confirm whether expanded coverage would have surfaced latent syntax errors elsewhere requiring fixes in the same diff.

quality.rationale: Implementation is minimal, readable, and scoped to the single required check file with an explicit glob array and a nullglob comment. Deductions for redundant two-loop file collection (globs already expand at array-assignment time, making the inner re-expansion loop unnecessary and slightly misleading), unquoted inner for expansion that would word-split unusual filenames, stderr suppression on bash -n failures, no defensive [[ -f ]] guard before bash -n, and no inline comments documenting bats exclusion or glob-set rationale.

Bundle contains no verification notes, bash test.sh output, narrow syntax-check output, negative-smoke demonstration or explanation, or documented no-change doc-sync decision required by acceptance criteria, so full plan/verification discipline cannot be confirmed from bundle evidence alone.

Bundle lacks full_test_sh execution evidence (skipped in bundle-only grading), no reported command output, and no negative-smoke test or explanation that a deliberate syntax error is caught and cleared, leaving verification discipline thin despite plausible wiring.
